newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen edging higher after Greenspan's comments.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen edging higher after Greenspan's comments.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to have an upward bias on Wednesday following U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Congressional testimony.
"U.S. Treasuries rose considerably after Greenspan's comments...and JGBs are likely to be firmer when trade opens," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.

The market will be focusing on the results of a 10-year JGB auction due at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT). If the coupon rate for the new 10-year issue is set at 2.5 percent as expected, demand from investors is likely to be modest, traders said.
"There are very few people with a strong appetite for the bonds at 2.5 percent," said a trader for a major brokerage house.
Even if there is only moderate initial demand for the new issue however, investors are likely to be eager to buy from the secondary market if the price is right, traders said.
"Investors are eager to buy on dips, which is why JGBs will probably have solid support near last week's low of 124.56," the first trader said.
If results of the 10-year bond auction are good, JGBs may try for a break above 125.50, the second trader said.
"If JGBs manage to break above 125.50, they may next try for 125.70," the trader said.
